question: Find all unit vectors parallel to $2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$. Explain why two answers are obtained.
explanation:
Step 1: Magnitude of the given vector
Let $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$. Its magnitude is
\(|\vec{a}|=\sqrt{2^2+2^2+(-1)^2}=3\)
Step 2: Unit vector in the same direction
\(\frac{\vec{a}}{|\vec{a}|}=\frac{2}{3}\hat{i}+\frac{2}{3}\hat{j}-\frac{1}{3}\hat{k}\)
Step 3: Unit vector in the opposite direction
The negative of this unit vector is also parallel to $\vec{a}$:
\(-\frac{2}{3}\hat{i}-\frac{2}{3}\hat{j}+\frac{1}{3}\hat{k}\)
Step 4: Interpretation
A line has two opposite directions. Therefore, two unit vectors parallel to the given vector are possible.
Final Answer
The required unit vectors are $\pm\left(\frac{2}{3}\hat{i}+\frac{2}{3}\hat{j}-\frac{1}{3}\hat{k}\right)$.

options.A: The only unit vector parallel to the given vector is $\frac{2}{3}\hat{i}+\frac{2}{3}\hat{j}-\frac{1}{3}\hat{k}$.
options.B: The unit vectors are $\pm\left(\frac{2}{3}\hat{i}+\frac{2}{3}\hat{j}-\frac{1}{3}\hat{k}\right)$; two answers arise because parallel vectors may point in either of two opposite directions.
options.C: The unit vectors are $\pm(2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})$ because the given vector is already a unit vector.
